The ATT is about **4.14** using regression adjustment: fit an outcome model on the control group, predict each treated child's counterfactual outcome, and average the differences.

Estimates depend on the method, so here is the spread:

| Estimator | ATT |
|---|---|
| Naive difference in means | 4.23 |
| Regression adjustment (outcome model on controls) | **4.14** |
| Doubly robust (AIPW) | 4.12 |
| Inverse probability weighting | 4.22 |
| Propensity-score 1-NN matching | 4.20 |
| Covariate 1-NN matching | 4.44 |

The model-based estimates (regression adjustment, doubly robust, IPW) all fall between 4.12 and 4.22. I chose regression adjustment as the direct estimator of the treated-group effect. Rounding to the nearest hundredth gives 4.14. Question.md doesn't name a method, so if a specific one is expected, the answer could differ slightly.

ANSWER: 4.14
